task_summary: Define the interface contract for the PipelineDiagram component — a React/SVG component rendering the exemplar.tools pipeline flow (Steps 0–7) with branching parallel steps (1a/1b, 2a/2b, 5a/5b/5c), clickable navigation via React Router, and responsive sizing. Must use the canonical PipelineNode/PipelineNodeList types and integrate with RouteSlug, StepId, StepLabel enums. Named export only. TypeScript strict mode with vitest tests.

findings.topic: SVG Pipeline/DAG Layout Patterns in React
findings.finding: Best practice for pipeline diagrams in React is to separate the layout data (node positions, edges) from the rendering layer. Nodes are defined as a typed array with x/y coordinates, and edges/connections are derived from the node ordering rather than hardcoded. The SVG viewBox attribute enables responsive scaling without manual resize listeners — use a fixed coordinate system (e.g., viewBox='0 0 1200 600') and let the browser scale. This avoids imperative resize logic and works well with Tailwind's width/height utilities on the outer container.
findings.source: React SVG component patterns; d3-dag and react-flow architectural patterns
findings.relevance: Directly applicable — PipelineNode already has x/y fields, and the component needs responsive sizing.

findings.topic: Canonical Type Reuse — PipelineNode and PipelineNodeList
findings.finding: The registry defines PipelineNode with fields {stepId: StepId, label: StepLabel, slug: RouteSlug, x: number, y: number} and PipelineNodeList as an array of PipelineNode. These MUST be used as-is. The component's props should accept PipelineNodeList (or derive it internally from a constant). Additional component-specific types (e.g., PipelineEdge for arrow connections, PipelineDiagramProps for the component's prop interface) should be defined separately without shadowing or redefining canonical types.
findings.source: Canonical Type Registry in project spec
findings.relevance: Critical — the operating procedures forbid redefining registry types with different fields.

findings.finding: The pipeline has a non-linear topology: Step 0 → (1a, 1b) → (2a, 2b) → 3 → 4 → (5a, 5b, 5c) → 6 → 7. A PipelineEdge type {from: StepId, to: StepId} cleanly models this. The edge list should be a module-level constant, not passed as props, since the topology is fixed. SVG <line> or <path> elements connect node centers. For branching, a fan-out/fan-in pattern with simple polylines or curved paths (quadratic Bézier via SVG 'Q' command) is clearest visually.
findings.source: Common DAG visualization patterns; CI/CD pipeline UI conventions
findings.relevance: Directly applicable — the branching structure (1a/1b, 2a/2b, 5a/5b/5c) requires explicit edge definitions.

findings.topic: React Router Navigation from SVG Elements
findings.finding: Clickable SVG elements should use React Router's useNavigate() hook rather than wrapping in <Link>. SVG <g> elements with onClick handlers and role='link' + tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown (Enter/Space) provide accessible click targets. Alternatively, wrapping each node group in a <foreignObject> containing a React Router <Link> works but is less reliable cross-browser. The useNavigate approach is the standard pattern. The slug handling guard (slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug) must be applied before calling navigate().
findings.source: React Router v6 docs; WAI-ARIA SVG accessibility guidelines
findings.relevance: Critical — each step box must be clickable and navigate to the correct route. The operating procedures explicitly require slug guard logic.

findings.finding: Per operating procedures, ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values already include a leading slash. The contract must document that PipelineNode.slug values come from RouteSlug (which already has leading slashes). The guard `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug` should still be applied defensively in the navigate handler, but the type contract should note that double-slash bugs are a known pitfall.
findings.source: Project Operating Procedures — Slug Handling section
findings.relevance: Directly required by project rules. Failure to guard causes broken navigation.

findings.finding: Each clickable node should have: (1) role='link', (2) tabIndex={0}, (3) aria-label with the step label, (4) cursor: pointer styling, (5) keyboard event handling for Enter and Space. The overall SVG should have role='img' with an aria-label describing it as a pipeline diagram, plus a <title> element for screen readers. Focus indicators should be visible (outline or stroke change on :focus-visible).
findings.source: WAI-ARIA 1.2 spec; WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines for interactive SVG
findings.relevance: Important for accessibility compliance and good UX practice.

findings.topic: Component Props Design — Minimal vs Configurable
findings.finding: Since the pipeline topology is fixed (always 13 steps in the same structure), the best pattern is to have PipelineDiagram accept zero required props — the node list and edge list are internal constants. Optional props for className, testId, and an onNodeClick callback (for testing or custom behavior) provide flexibility. The onNodeClick callback also makes testing easier: tests can assert click behavior without mocking useNavigate. However, providing a nodes prop as optional allows storybook/test overrides.
findings.source: React component design best practices; testing-library patterns
findings.relevance: Directly applicable — simplifies the public API while enabling testability.

findings.topic: Testing Clickable SVG Nodes with vitest + testing-library
findings.finding: Use @testing-library/react's render + screen.getByRole('link', {name: 'Step 0 — Cartographer'}) to find nodes. For navigation testing, mock useNavigate via vi.mock('react-router-dom') and assert navigate was called with the correct slug. Per project rules, the vi.mock() factory must provide ALL named exports of react-router-dom that the module uses. Common pitfall: forgetting to mock useLocation or other hooks that react-router-dom re-exports. Using MemoryRouter wrapper is the simpler alternative that avoids extensive mocking.
findings.source: vitest docs; @testing-library/react patterns; project vi.mock() rules
findings.relevance: Critical — tests must verify all 13 step nodes render and click navigation works, per the task description.

findings.finding: Use a fixed viewBox (e.g., '0 0 1200 500') and set width='100%' with preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' on the <svg> element. The outer container div uses Tailwind classes (w-full, max-w-screen-xl, mx-auto) for responsive behavior. No JavaScript resize listeners needed. Node x/y coordinates in PipelineNode are in viewBox coordinate space. This is the standard responsive SVG pattern.
findings.source: MDN SVG viewBox docs; responsive SVG best practices
findings.relevance: Directly applicable for responsive sizing requirement.

findings.topic: Named Export Convention and Module Structure
findings.finding: Per project standards: named exports only, no default exports. The module should export: PipelineDiagram (component), PipelineDiagramProps (type), PipelineEdge (type if defined), PIPELINE_NODES (constant), PIPELINE_EDGES (constant). Use 'export type { }' for type-only exports. The component file should be pipeline-diagram.tsx with a co-located pipeline-diagram.test.tsx.

The canonical registry does not define a PipelineEdge type. This is a component-specific type that should be defined in the pipeline_diagram module. Recommended shape: { from: StepId; to: StepId }. This is clean, minimal, and uses the canonical StepId enum. An optional 'id' or 'label' field is unnecessary for this use case.
findings.source: Canonical Type Registry analysis; graph data modeling conventions
findings.relevance: Needed to model the DAG edges; must be defined as a new type without conflicting with registry types.

findings.topic: Home Node Exclusion from Pipeline Diagram
findings.finding: StepId includes 'home' but the pipeline diagram shows Steps 0–7 only. The PipelineNode list should contain 12 nodes (cartographer through kindex), not 13. The 'home' StepId should be excluded from PIPELINE_NODES. This is an easy-to-miss edge case — the diagram is displayed ON the home page but doesn't include home as a pipeline step.
findings.source: Task description analysis — 'Renders step boxes (Step 0 through Step 7)'
findings.relevance: Critical edge case — including 'home' as a pipeline node would be incorrect.

recommended_approach:
Define the PipelineDiagram contract as follows:

1. **Canonical types used as-is**: PipelineNode, PipelineNodeList, StepId, StepLabel, RouteSlug — imported from their owning modules, never redefined.

2. **New component-specific types**:
   - `PipelineEdge`: `{ from: StepId; to: StepId }` — models a directed connection between two pipeline steps.
   - `PipelineEdgeList`: `PipelineEdge[]` — all edges in the DAG.
   - `PipelineDiagramProps`: `{ className?: string; nodes?: PipelineNodeList; edges?: PipelineEdgeList; onNodeClick?: (slug: RouteSlug) => void }` — all optional for maximum flexibility. Defaults to internal constants.

3. **Module constants**:
   - `PIPELINE_NODES`: PipelineNodeList — 12 nodes (excluding 'home'), each with stepId, label, slug, x, y in viewBox coordinates.
   - `PIPELINE_EDGES`: PipelineEdgeList — explicit edge list modeling the DAG: 0→1a, 0→1b, 1a→2a, 1b→2b (or merged converge at 3), 2a→3, 2b→3, 3→4, 4→5a, 4→5b, 4→5c, 5a→6, 5b→6, 5c→6, 6→7.

4. **Component behavior**:
   - Renders an SVG with fixed viewBox, responsive via width='100%' and preserveAspectRatio.
   - Each node is a `<g>` with rect + text, onClick calls navigate(guardedSlug) or the onNodeClick prop.
   - Edges rendered as SVG `<line>` or `<path>` elements.
   - Accessible: role='link', tabIndex, aria-label, keyboard support on each node.
   - Slug guard applied: `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug`.

5. **Exports**: Named only — `export { PipelineDiagram, PIPELINE_NODES, PIPELINE_EDGES }` and `export type { PipelineDiagramProps, PipelineEdge, PipelineEdgeList }`.

6. **Tests**: Wrap in MemoryRouter, verify all 12 step nodes render by aria-label, verify click on each triggers navigation to the correct slug. Use vi.mock for useNavigate to capture calls.
alternatives_considered: Use react-flow or dagre library for automatic layout — rejected because the pipeline is a fixed, small DAG (12 nodes) and adding a heavy dependency is unnecessary. Hand-positioned nodes via PipelineNode x/y is simpler and more controllable.
Pass nodes and edges as required props — rejected in favor of internal constants since the pipeline topology is fixed. Optional props for override/testing is sufficient.
Use <foreignObject> with React Router <Link> for clickable nodes — rejected due to cross-browser inconsistencies. useNavigate() with onClick on SVG <g> elements is more reliable.
Use a <canvas> element instead of SVG — rejected because SVG provides built-in accessibility, responsive scaling via viewBox, and easier testing with DOM queries.
Define edges implicitly from node array ordering — rejected because the branching topology (fan-out/fan-in) cannot be inferred from a flat list. Explicit PipelineEdge[] is necessary.
Wrap the entire SVG in a single React Router <Link> — rejected because each node needs individual navigation to different routes.
risks: Mismatch between StepId enum values and the node list — if enum values change upstream, the constant PIPELINE_NODES silently becomes stale. Mitigate with a type-level exhaustiveness check or a test that asserts PIPELINE_NODES covers all non-home StepId values.

Double-slash bug if slug guard is omitted or applied incorrectly — RouteSlug values already have leading slashes, so naively prepending '/' creates '//step-0-cartographer'. The guard must be applied exactly as specified in operating procedures.
SVG coordinate brittleness — hardcoded x/y positions in PipelineNode may look wrong at certain aspect ratios. Mitigate by using viewBox with preserveAspectRatio and testing at multiple widths.

vi.mock('react-router-dom') incomplete mock — per project rules, the mock factory must export every named runtime export used by the component. Missing useNavigate, useLocation, MemoryRouter, etc. will cause test failures. Prefer wrapping in MemoryRouter + spying on navigate over full module mocking where possible.
Accessibility regression — SVG click targets without proper role, tabIndex, and keyboard handlers will be inaccessible. Must be part of the contract and tested.
Node count off-by-one — the 'home' StepId exists but must NOT appear in the pipeline diagram. Tests should assert exactly 12 nodes.
compliance_notes: All source files must be .ts or .tsx — component in pipeline-diagram.tsx, tests in pipeline-diagram.test.tsx
TypeScript strict mode required — all public functions must have type annotations
Named exports only — no default exports. Use 'export type { }' for type-only exports
Canonical types PipelineNode, PipelineNodeList, StepId, StepLabel, RouteSlug must be used exactly as defined in the registry — no field additions or renames
vi.mock() factories must provide every named runtime export of the mocked module
Slug guard required: slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug — must be applied before navigation
All functions must have at least one test; tests must run without external services
Import from sibling modules using exact exported names — never guess
Prefer composition over inheritance — PipelineDiagram should compose SVG elements, not extend a base class
